extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community (applicants, investigators, program administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: A news/index page summarizing recent NIH policy updates, resources, and reminders relevant to grant applicants and awardees (e.g., model selection guidance, new application formats, data-sharing plan formats, peer-review changes). Meant to alert readers to topics they should follow for application preparation and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate experimental models
rubrics_metrics.description: "NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance our understanding of human health and disease. As we continue to encourage approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose models (including New Approach Methodologies/NAMs) that are scientifically sound and most appropriate to the research question; prioritize human relevance and translational potential where appropriate. The statement serves as policy guidance to justify model choice in applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects — application format and linked awards
rubrics_metrics.description: "Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants to PF5 should follow the specified application format and be prepared for the possibility that an application could be split into linked awards after peer review and before Just-in-Time (JIT) requests. Use the NIH overview video/resource to learn key features and administrative expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS plans for relevant applications, use the updated 2026 Pilot format and include the simplified set of required elements specified by NIH. This is a procedural requirement and affects plan structure and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication and reproducibility expectations in applications
rubrics_metrics.description: "The reliability of biomedical research is foundational to public trust in science and to ensuring that findings can benefit patients and communities. NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility. In support of this plan, NIH has launched a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize and institutionalize replication and reproducibility efforts across the biomedical research enterprise."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should embed considerations of replication and reproducibility throughout applications and proposed work (methods, study design, data-sharing, validation plans). Expect NIH to prioritize and potentially incentivize replication/reproducibility efforts; consult initiative-related guidance when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding the 'Competitive But Not Discussed' scoring designation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that, under NIH emergency modifications described, applications ranked in the middle third of a study section could be labeled 'competitive but not discussed' — indicating they were scored as competitive yet not discussed at full study section. This affects how applicants interpret review outcomes and next-step actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralization of NIH peer review within CSR
rubrics_metrics.description: "In March 2025, NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) ... As the one-year anniversary approaches, we are providing an update on the consolidation and its initial effects on the peer-review process."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and reviewers should recognize that peer review processes and administrative handling are consolidated under CSR; expect changes in review logistics, potential impacts on efficiency, competition, and transparency. Consult CSR/NIH notices for specific operational or timing effects on submission and review.
